about: The defect classes the landing review has stopped PRs for, and how each shows in a diff. This file does not decide what is checked: core/tests/recurring_defects.py counts each class's `finding` regex over the recorded LAND-AFTER-FIX reviews and checks only a class found on 2 or more distinct PRs. `example` is a finding the record holds; `path`, `added`, `unless` (the file as it now stands) and `unless_added` (the diff's added lines in that file) are the shape; `red` and `clean` are the fixtures the selftest runs every class against.

classes.name: pause-hold-missing
classes.example: holds() never asks `cc-pause is <repo>`, so on a parked project the tick still runs `cc-board add`
classes.what: launches a worker or writes the board, and nothing in the file asks whether the project is paused (cc-pause is <repo>)

red.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# start every ready row
for row in $(ready "$repo"); do
  cc "$repo" "$row" --go "$(brief "$row")"
done

clean.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# start every ready row
cc-pause is "$repo" >/dev/null && exit 0
for row in $(ready "$repo"); do
  cc "$repo" "$row" --go "$(brief "$row")"
done

classes.name: held-files-unchecked
classes.example: a running bundle row with no commit yet holds no files, so `go` starts a second worker in the file the live bundle is editing
classes.what: dispatches or groups rows, and nothing in the file checks the files a live track already holds (held_files)

classes.name: kill-fence-spelling
classes.example: every argument starting with `-` is skipped as 'a signal', so a negative pid given to kill is never fenced
classes.what: changes how a kill is fenced with no new selfcheck case beside it; each time, the review found the next spelling past the fence

red.text: NOEXEC="nice nohup timeout"   # heads that run their argument, so a kill behind them is fenced too

clean.text:
NOEXEC="nice nohup timeout"   # heads that run their argument, so a kill behind them is fenced too
ok "a kill behind nohup is fenced like a bare one" "$r"
